voice: ElevenLabs eleven_v4, Jack (BVPhWQykET1TSvfGzrUr), English, one take, split into lines, inner pauses capped at 0.22 s, no tempo change; the door voice is Alden (S9V0fuqWOqX0i8Kb8ctu), take 1

lines.text: The summer I turned fifteen, I watched a white hat drift along the top of my grandparents' hedge. That hedge is eight feet tall.
lines.beat_before: hook: summer daylight, the tall hedge; a white hat glides along its top, stops where I stand, tilts

lines.text: When I told Grandpa, the colour left his face. By dark they had sealed me upstairs. Paper over every window. A bowl of salt in each corner.
lines.beat_before: Grandpa turns; Grandma pastes newspaper over the window, salt bowls in the corners

lines.text: "Don't open that door before sunrise. Whatever you hear."
lines.beat_before: Grandma at the sliding door, closing it on me and Grandpa

lines.text: Around two, the salt started turning black. Then something tapped on every window at once. On the second floor.
lines.beat_before: silent night: the sealed room, one bulb; the salt in the near bowl darkens grain by grain (the viewer sees it first)

lines.text: Then, through the door, Grandpa's voice.
lines.beat_before: the tapping runs round every papered window; the papers dent inward; "po po po" outside

lines.text: It's all over now. You can come out. Open the door for Grandpa.
lines.beat_before: the door: on its paper, a shadow far too tall folds down at the waist to the height of a man

lines.text: But Grandpa was sitting right beside me. And he was shaking his head.
lines.beat_before: Grandpa beside me, his hand on my shoulder, slowly shaking his head; the shadow tilts its head to listen

lines.text: At dawn they drove me out of the valley. She walked beside the car the whole way, bent down to my window. I didn't look. Not once.
lines.beat_before: dawn: the car on the valley road; she strides beside it, bent double, her face at my window; her smile
